title: iter-3 price injection uses naive >>64n; bid prices come out inverted (still wrong)
description: Iter-3 added `price = Number(BigInt(orderIdStr) >> 64n)` claiming this 'Holds for both bids and asks in DeepBook v3.' That claim contradicts the project's own chain-shape.md (lines 137-145), which states: 'For asks the encoding is monotonically increasing in price; for bids it is decreasing (inverted price)'. The patch performs only a right-shift; it does NOT invert for bids, and it does NOT mask off bit 63 of the shifted result for asks (the ask flag bit becomes the high bit of the shifted u64 → ~9.22e18 dominates the Number cast). Net effect: every bid carries a fabricated huge or zero price, every ask carries (price | 2^63). computeMarketStats then sorts bids by these fabricated values and the 'best bid' is the bid whose order_id had the LOWEST price (i.e. truly the WORST bid), and best ask is whichever ask happens to sort first by askBit-poisoned values.
impact: R3-014 (iter-2) is NOT fixed; it has been replaced by a different equally-silent garbage path. Mid-price = (worstBid + askWithFlagBit) / 2 — the user sees a giant scientific-notation number that looks like data. AC1.4's bestBid <= mid <= bestAsk invariant holds only because both sides are corrupted in the same direction. The synthesis-notes' claim 'production reads the correct chain price instead of falling through to decodeBidPrice' is false. iter-3 should have been a 1-line wrapper around the EXISTING decodeAskPrice/decodeBidPrice helpers in marketStats.ts (which already do the bit-masking and inversion correctly) — instead it duplicated and inlined a wrong version of the math.
recommendation: Either (a) import decodeAskPrice/decodeBidPrice from marketStats.ts and call the correct one based on order_id's high bit, or (b) inline the correct math: `const id = BigInt(orderIdStr); const isAsk = (id >> 127n) === 1n; const raw = (id & ((1n<<127n)-1n)) >> 64n; price = isAsk ? Number(raw) : Number(((1n<<64n)-1n) - raw);`. Test the patched function against the actual bid example from chain-shape.md (`18446744073709548345`) — current code returns 0, correct code returns U64_MAX-0 inverted appropriately.

title: iter-3 try/catch silently swallows BigInt parse failure to undefined
description: The new try/catch around BigInt(orderIdStr) catches parse failures and sets price = undefined with no log, no count, no signal. Once the bad-shape order is pushed with `price: undefined`, computeMarketStats falls through to decodeAskPrice/decodeBidPrice — which call BigInt(orderId) again on the SAME unparseable string and throw synchronously (R3-007 from iter-2 — those decoders have no try/catch). So the iter-3 try/catch only delays the crash by one frame, AND silently masks the original parse error from any operator-visible diagnostic. The catch{} also hides the typical 'isFinite is false' case (orderIdStr too large for Number-after-shift) which is a meaningful signal: a u128 with bits 64-127 set above 2^53 means precision was lost in the Number cast — silently substituting undefined hides that.
impact: When a real chain returns an order_id that BigInt cannot parse (chain-shape drift, a malformed wrapper response), the user sees either '—' (if marketStats happens to also bail) or a SyntaxError thrown from decodeBidPrice — neither names the original orderIdStr, the slice, or the pool. Latent: probably never fires on the happy path. Low because the deeper R3-001 bug means this code is wrong anyway and rewriting it will subsume this finding.
recommendation: When the rewrite for R3-001 happens, either (a) at least console.warn the orderIdStr that failed before setting price=undefined, or (b) skip pushing the order entirely if its price is unrecoverable (don't poison the book with a price-less order that a downstream decoder will then crash on).

title: manifest.ts loadManifest still rewrites all fs errors to 'not found'
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (carry-over from iter-2 R3-001). The catch around fs.readFile still rewrites EACCES, EISDIR, EMFILE all to 'Deployment manifest not found at <path>'. Original error is dropped — no `cause`, no errno, no console.error. parseManifest extraction (iter-2) was good but loadManifest's I/O error path was untouched in iter-3.
impact: Operator with a permissions issue gets pointed at `pnpm deploy-all`, which won't fix it. Affects only Node-side test/CLI tooling now; production browser path uses the Vite middleware (vite.config.ts has the same single-message problem at lines 38-45 — see R3-016).
recommendation: Discriminate on `(err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code`: only claim 'not found' for ENOENT, otherwise emit `Deployment manifest at ${path} unreadable: ${code}` with `{ cause: err }`.

title: manifest.ts loadManifest JSON.parse still unguarded; raw SyntaxError thrown
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-002 carry-over). After fs.readFile succeeds, line 105 calls `JSON.parse(raw) as unknown` with no try/catch. parseManifest validates AFTER parse, but a malformed JSON payload (truncated mid-write by `pnpm deploy-all`, BOM, accidental edit) still throws raw `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ... in JSON at position N` with no manifest path, no bootstrap hint, no actionable message.
impact: AC1.2 actionable-error guarantee bypassed for the malformed-JSON case. Same problem exists in main.tsx response.json() path (R3-013) and in vite.config.ts middleware (it serves bytes without validating they parse).
recommendation: Wrap line 105: `try { return parseManifest(JSON.parse(raw), manifestPath); } catch (err) { if (err instanceof SyntaxError) throw new Error(`Deployment manifest at ${manifestPath} is not valid JSON: ${err.message}. ${BOOTSTRAP_HINT}`); throw err; }`.
evidence:
const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as unknown;
  return parseManifest(parsed, manifestPath);

title: main.tsx silently no-ops when #root element is missing
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-003 carry-over). If document.getElementById('root') returns null (broken index.html, hot-reload race, mismatched id), the `if (root)` guard silently skips createRoot/render. Blank page, no console error.
impact: Blank page with zero diagnostic. Low because index.html is correct today; the silent-skip default is the wrong choice for a fatal mounting precondition.
recommendation: `if (!root) throw new Error('main.tsx: #root missing in index.html');`. Or at minimum console.error.

title: rpc() does not check response.ok; non-2xx produces opaque JSON-parse error
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-004 carry-over). `rpc()` calls `await response.json()` without first asserting `response.ok` or status. A 502/503 from the Sui RPC port, a 404 from a wrong path, or an HTML error page from a misconfigured proxy throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0` rather than the actionable RPC-unreachable error AC1.1/T-020 promises.
impact: Sandbox-down or sandbox-restart-mid-cycle (a contract-acknowledged failure mode) surfaces as opaque JSON parse errors instead of an actionable 'Sui RPC unreachable; run pnpm deploy-all'. Per-pool, propagated through Promise.allSettled in App.tsx — user sees the same opaque error N times in the alert banner.
recommendation: Before `await response.json()`: `if (!response.ok) throw new Error(\`Sui RPC ${method} returned HTTP ${response.status} from ${rpcUrl}. Verify the sandbox is running.\`);`. Wrap the json() call in try/catch too.

title: rpc() does not handle network-level fetch rejection (DNS, ECONNREFUSED)
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-005 carry-over). The fetch() call has no try/catch; the most common sandbox-down case (port closed → `TypeError: Failed to fetch`) propagates verbatim. The error message names neither the RPC URL nor the bootstrap recipe.
impact: The most user-visible failure mode (sandbox not running) gets the least actionable error. Worsened by iter-2 Promise.allSettled wrap: the user sees one identical, opaque 'Failed to fetch' line per pool, multiplying noise without adding signal.
recommendation: Wrap fetch in try/catch and rethrow with a wrapped, actionable message including rpcUrl and bootstrap hint, attaching the original via `{ cause: err }`.

title: rpc() casts result to T without checking env.result is defined
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-006 carry-over). After the env.error guard, `return env.result as T` proceeds even if env.result is undefined. Downstream callers (resolvePoolInnerFields, traverseBigVector, buildQueryEventsFn) then read fields off undefined/empty objects via ?. and ?? defaults, silently producing empty books / no fills.
impact: An aberrant or partial JSON-RPC response (proxy injection, edge-case server impl) results in silent empty data instead of an explicit error. The fallback chains in resolvePoolInnerFields (returns null → buildPoolInnerState skipped → empty Book) make the path even more silent than in iter-1.
recommendation: After the env.error branch: `if (env.result === undefined) throw new Error(\`${method} returned no result and no error\`);`.

title: computeMarketStats decoders still unguarded BigInt; Number(quantity) NaN-poisons depth
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-007 carry-over). decodeAskPrice/decodeBidPrice still call `BigInt(orderId)` with no try/catch; a non-numeric order_id (chain-shape drift, dataLayer fallback string '0' from R3-008-style undefined) throws synchronous SyntaxError. Number(o.quantity) on lines 50/56 still has no Number.isFinite guard; non-numeric quantities silently become NaN and every NaN level then fails `lvl.price >= lo && lvl.price <= hi` (NaN comparisons always false) so depth silently drops affected levels. The iter-3 try/catch around the *new* BigInt call in dataLayer.ts (line 211) does NOT protect this older call site — the same orderIdStr that defaulted to '0' in iter-3 will hit decodeBidPrice fine (BigInt('0') doesn't throw) but produce decoded price = U64_MAX, which then sorts as the BEST bid — silent garbage.
impact: BigInt throw is a hard-crash path, fully reachable in production now via the iter-2 wiring. The iter-3 default-to-'0' on missing order_id (dataLayer.ts line 209) is particularly bad: an order with no order_id silently becomes the best bid at price ~1.8e19 (U64_MAX-0 inverted), distorting mid by a factor of ~1e16.
recommendation: Wrap order-id decode in try/catch and skip orders that fail (with optional console.warn). After Number(), guard `Number.isFinite(qty)` and skip non-finite levels. Also: never default order_id to '0' in dataLayer; skip the order instead.

title: aggregateFills coerces fill price/quantity via Number() with no NaN guard
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-008 carry-over). aggregateFills sums `Number(f.baseQuantity)` into volume24h and casts `Number(sorted[last].price)` for lastPrice without guarding NaN. A single malformed fill record (chain-shape drift, missing field) poisons the whole day's volume (NaN + N = NaN for the rest of the loop) and lastPrice silently becomes NaN. PoolCard's fmt sentinel masks the symptom — user sees '—' for ALL trades when only one was malformed.
impact: Single bad fill corrupts whole-day volume. Silent: '—' looks identical to 'no trades'. Reachable via the live data layer.
recommendation: `const q = Number(f.baseQuantity); if (Number.isFinite(q)) volume24h += q;` and similarly for price. Optional: count and surface malformedFills.

title: fetchFills loop has no upper bound on pagination; misbehaving RPC could spin forever
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-009 carry-over). fetchFills uses `while (true)` with three break conditions but no maximum-iteration safety bound. If queryEvents returns hasNextPage:true indefinitely while always returning data old-but-not-quite (so neither MAX_FILLS nor crossedWindow fires) or returns the same cursor, fetchFills hangs forever and App stays in 'loading' status with no signal.
impact: Hung loading state with no timeout. Combined with the setInterval refresh (App.tsx line 94, R3-018), a hung fetchFills will block subsequent refresh cycles' Promise.allSettled.
recommendation: Add hard iteration cap: `for (let i = 0; i < 200; i++)` and throw 'queryEvents pagination exceeded N pages without satisfying stop conditions' if reached. Also detect cursor-no-advance.

title: fetchFills assumes response.data iterable; non-array throws non-actionable TypeError
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-010 carry-over). fillFetcher assumes response.data is iterable. dataLayer.ts buildQueryEventsFn defends with `result.data ?? []` (the production path through is safe), but the QueryEventsFn type signature allows custom impls returning `data: undefined` (R3-008 means rpc() can return undefined). `for (const ev of response.data)` then throws `TypeError: response.data is not iterable`.
impact: Edge-case crash with non-actionable error. Lower risk than iter-1 because dataLayer.ts now defends, but the contract is fragile.
recommendation: `if (!Array.isArray(response.data)) throw new Error('queryEvents returned non-array data field');` at top of loop body.
evidence:
for (const ev of response.data) {
      if (ev.poolId !== poolId) continue;

title: PoolCard fmt() uses String(value); fine numerics render as scientific notation
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-011 carry-over). fmt() returns `String(value)` for finite numbers; very small or very large values render as scientific notation (e.g. '1.23e-8') which a non-technical user might misread as the sentinel. Especially relevant given R3-001: the iter-3-broken price decode produces values around 9.22e18 for asks — those will literally render as '9.223372036854776e+18' in the UI.
impact: Cosmetic / latent UX bug. Not load-bearing for any AC. Now also a leakage path for the R3-001 garbage-price values to surface visibly to the user as obviously-broken numbers.
recommendation: Mirror sparkline's toFixed approach: `value.toLocaleString(undefined, { maximumFractionDigits: 6 })` or pin per-field toFixed.

title: main.tsx fetch + response.json() unguarded against network or parse errors
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-013 carry-over). main.tsx loadManifest does NOT wrap `fetch(MANIFEST_URL)` in try/catch (network failure → raw TypeError) nor `await response.json()` (malformed JSON → raw SyntaxError). The Vite middleware can serve malformed JSON if the manifest file itself is malformed (the middleware does no parse-validation, just reads bytes — see vite.config.ts:34-37). A truncated/corrupted manifest then surfaces as `SyntaxError: Unexpected token...` directly into App's error UI without any indication this is a manifest-shape problem.
impact: AC1.1/AC1.2 actionable-error guarantee bypassed in the browser path for the same two failure modes parseManifest defends against in the validation step.
recommendation: Wrap `await response.json()` in try/catch and rethrow as 'Deployment manifest at /localnet.json is not valid JSON: ...'. Same pattern fixes R3-004.

title: traverseBigVector silently swallows all per-slice fetch errors with bare catch+continue
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-015 carry-over). The `try { ... } catch { continue; }` around per-slice sui_getObject is bare — no error is logged, no count is kept, no signal emitted. If ALL slices fail (e.g. RPC down, packageId wrong), traverseBigVector returns `[]` and the pool's book becomes silently empty. computeMarketStats then returns mid/spread/depth all undefined and the user sees '—' for every metric — looking identical to a genuinely empty pool.
impact: Silent total failure of book reads renders identically to a healthy idle pool. iter-1 R3-005 'silent stub' is structurally back. Operator can't distinguish 'sandbox is idle' from 'all slice fetches failing'.
recommendation: Track failed-slice count and either log via console.warn (`'%d/%d BigVector slices failed for pool %s'`) or thread the count up so PoolCard can show a 'partial data' indicator. At minimum: `} catch (err) { failedSlices++; continue; }` plus a final guard `if (failedSlices === sliceList.data.length && sliceList.data.length > 0) throw new Error(...)`.

title: resolvePoolInnerFields null path silently fabricates an empty book
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-016 carry-over). fetchPoolStats checks `if (innerFields)` and on null falls through to `poolState = { pool_id: descriptor.poolId, book: { asks: [], bids: [], lot_size: '0', min_size: '0', tick_size: '0' } }` — a hardcoded empty book with NO error, NO log, NO signal. resolvePoolInnerFields returns null in TWO places (lines 113-114 missing fields, 144 missing wrapper) — distinct failure modes (object deleted, wrong objectId, dynamic-field traversal failure) the user has zero visibility into. The empty-book result then flows through computeMarketStats producing mid/spread/depth all undefined — rendering '—' for every metric — identical to either an idle pool or a successfully-read empty pool.
impact: Same silent-empty pattern as R3-015 but at the outer level. A pool object that exists but is mid-upgrade, has been deleted, or whose wrapper shape has drifted produces '—' across the board with no operator-visible distinction from 'no orders on book'. AC1.1 'inline error UI' is bypassed entirely for this path. The dev WROTE the fallback knowing the fields might be missing, but never decided what the user should see.
recommendation: Either throw with an actionable message ('Pool ${descriptor.poolId} inner state unreadable — wrapper shape mismatch or object missing') so the per-pool error banner fires, or attach a `dataState: 'ok' | 'partial' | 'empty' | 'error'` field to PoolCardData so the UI can distinguish 'genuinely empty' from 'failed to read'.

title: buildQueryEventsFn coerces timestamp via Number() with 0 fallback; one bad event truncates pagination
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-017 carry-over). buildQueryEventsFn computes `const timestampMs = Number(j['timestamp'] ?? ev.timestampMs ?? 0)`. If both fields are missing or non-numeric, timestampMs becomes 0 (epoch). The fill is then pushed downstream with timestampMs=0, where fillFetcher's window check `nowMs - ev.timestampMs > DAY_MS` (line 67) is trivially true for nowMs > 86400000 (any modern clock), which sets `crossedWindow = true` and HALTS pagination after that page. Result: a single malformed event in a page truncates the entire fetch; subsequent in-window fills are never collected.
impact: One bad event per pool truncates that pool's fill stream. Volume24h drops to whatever was collected before the malformed event; sparkline truncates similarly. Silent: PoolCard renders the partial data without indicating it's partial. Worst case: malformed event is FIRST in descending-order response → entire pool's fill set is empty.
recommendation: Filter malformed events in buildQueryEventsFn: if parsed timestamp is non-finite or <= 0, skip the event (don't push) AND don't let it influence pagination. Alternatively, default to nowMs so malformed events are treated as 'still in window'.

title: App.tsx setInterval refresh has no in-flight guard; slow fetches stack and overlap
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-018 carry-over). The periodic-refresh effect (H-5 fix) uses `setInterval(async () => { ... await Promise.allSettled(...) }, 20_000)`. setInterval does NOT wait for the previous callback to resolve before firing. If a fetchPoolStats batch takes >20 s (entirely possible with R3-011's unbounded pagination, R3-007's no-timeout fetch, or just slow chain reads), a second batch starts while the first is in flight. Both batches setState; the second-to-resolve overwrites the first. With n pools and slow fetches, in-flight requests stack indefinitely.
impact: Under degraded RPC conditions, the SPA accumulates background fetches indefinitely. Memory/socket pressure on the browser; multiplied RPC load can worsen the sandbox's slowness. setState ordering non-deterministic — user may see stats flicker between fresh and stale.
recommendation: Track in-flight ref: `const inFlightRef = useRef(false); ... if (inFlightRef.current) return; inFlightRef.current = true; try { await ... } finally { inFlightRef.current = false; }`. Or replace setInterval with a self-rescheduling setTimeout that fires the next call only after the previous resolves.

title: App.tsx refresh interval setState fires after unmount; cancelled flag not honored
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-019 carry-over). The setInterval callback calls setState unconditionally on resolution; there is no `cancelled` ref equivalent to the initial-load effect (line 42). The cleanup function clears the interval, but a callback that was already in-flight when cleanup ran will still call setState after unmount. React 19 will warn ('Cannot update state on an unmounted component') and in strict-mode dev double-invocation this fires reliably.
impact: Console-warning noise + small leak (state of unmounted components held in closure). In production rare; in dev/testing pollutes the AC1.1 'no console errors' goal.
recommendation: Add a `cancelled` ref shared across both effects (or a single AbortController) and guard each setState behind `if (!cancelled.current) setState(...)`.

title: main.tsx cachedPackageId race — fragile rebinding of deps.loadManifest
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-020 carry-over). main.tsx threads packageId from manifest to fetchPoolStats via a module-level `let cachedPackageId = ''`. The override of deps.loadManifest assigns cachedPackageId AFTER the original loadManifest resolves. App.tsx's useEffect awaits loadManifest before calling fetchPoolStats, so the happy path is fine — but the design is fragile: the iter-2 setInterval refresh effect (line 94) calls deps.fetchPoolStats directly without re-checking that loadManifest already resolved. Any future refactor that triggers fetchPoolStats outside the initial-load gate will silently pass packageId='' to the data layer.
impact: Latent fragility, no current bug. The mutation pattern is non-obvious; a code reader might call fetchPoolStats from a new entry point and not realise the cache must be primed first.
recommendation: Either thread packageId through the descriptor (extend PoolDescriptor to include packageId, populated in loadManifest) or hold the manifest in a Promise and await it inside fetchPoolStats.

title: runDataLayer silently coerces missing packageId to empty string
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-021 carry-over). runDataLayer's `const packageId = manifest.packages?.deepbook?.packageId ?? '';` silently coerces a missing packageId to '' rather than throwing. The downstream queryEvents call then issues `{ MoveModule: { package: '', module: 'pool' } }` which the Sui RPC will reject — error eventually surfaces, but as a confusing JSON-RPC error rather than the validated 'manifest missing packages.deepbook.packageId' error parseManifest is designed to throw.
impact: Defensive gap. Silent fallback duplicates parseManifest's responsibility but doesn't enforce it. If a future caller bypasses parseManifest (e.g. constructs a manifest object inline for testing), the empty-string packageId silently flows to the chain.
recommendation: Add an explicit assertion at the top of runDataLayer: `if (!manifest.packages?.deepbook?.packageId) throw new Error('runDataLayer: manifest missing packages.deepbook.packageId');`. Better: change the manifest type to LoadedManifest (the validated shape).
evidence:
const pools = manifest.pools ?? {};
  const packageId = manifest.packages?.deepbook?.packageId ?? '';

title: Vite middleware 404 body discarded by main.tsx; per-environment disk path lost
description: Iter-2/iter-3 NOT FIXED (R3-012 carry-over). vite.config.ts (lines 38-45) catches the readFile error and returns a 404 with body `{"error": "localnet.json not found at <abs-path>. Run pnpm deploy-all from the deepbook-sandbox repo."}`. main.tsx checks `!response.ok` and throws its own message ('not reachable at /localnet.json. Run pnpm deploy-all ...') — the body is never read. The middleware took the trouble to compute and emit the absolute disk path and surface the precise reason, but main.tsx throws all that information away.
impact: AC1.2 'actionable error pointing at the bootstrap recipe' is partially satisfied — the message names `pnpm deploy-all` — but loses the per-environment specificity (the actual disk path the middleware tried) that would help diagnose 'is the sandbox checked out at the expected location?'. Two messages, one less informative than the other; the less-informative one wins.
recommendation: Have main.tsx read the response body on !response.ok and prefer the server's error message if present: `const body = await response.json().catch(() => null); throw new Error(body?.error ?? defaultMessage);`.
